prompt.context: Your client is the manufacturer of family oriented cars in the country Benelux. He only sells through dealers which he owns. He recently attended a seminar on customer loyalty and he wants you to find a way to solicit customer feedback and identify how loyal his customers are.
prompt.question: How would you design a system to solicit customer feedback and measure customer loyalty for this car manufacturer?

clarifying_info.q: What types of cars does the company make?
clarifying_info.a: The company makes a full range of cars.

clarifying_info.q: How is the company performing financially?
How many dealerships does the company have?
clarifying_info.a: He has 10 dealerships across the Benelux.

clarifying_info.q: Has the company done this kind of feedback collection before?
clarifying_info.a: He has never solicited this sort of feedback before.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have any existing customer data or infrastructure?
clarifying_info.a: The company does have a customer complaint department and does have a list of all their existing customers.

clarifying_info.q: Why do customers buy from this company?
clarifying_info.a: People buy from them because they have good cars and they like to buy a local car.

clarifying_info.q: How does the company price relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: The company charges a slight premium over the big players.

framework: 1. Understand the scale and scope of the business
2. Identify areas where customers come into contact with the company (garages, forecourts, annual maintenance checks, customer complaint department)
3. Identify what sort of information you want to collect — e.g., critical incident analysis, switching path analysis, lifetime value of customers
4. Identify how you are going to collect it — letters, phone calls, standing at garages, internet feedback forum, focus groups

questions.prompt: What specific survey questions would you ask customers to assess loyalty and satisfaction?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should include questions that probe: feature preferences (trade-off questions), competitive benchmarking on key attributes, repurchase intent, and qualitative incident recall. Examples: 'What do you value more on our car — 5 doors or air conditioning?'; 'How do you compare our car to a Volvo in terms of safety?'; 'Would you buy a car from us again?'; 'Can you give us an example of behavior at the forecourt which you can remember?'

brainstorming.prompt: What are the different ways you could collect customer feedback and measure loyalty for this car manufacturer?

categories.name: Survey channels
ideas: Direct mail letters to existing customer list
Internet feedback forum or online survey

categories.name: Types of loyalty/feedback data
ideas: Switching path analysis (why they left or stayed)
Lifetime value of customers (repeat purchase history)
Net Promoter Score or repurchase intent

recommendation: Design a structured customer feedback program leveraging the existing customer list and 10 dealerships as primary data collection points
Use a mix of channels (mail survey, in-dealership intercepts, online forum) to reach different customer segments and maximize response rates
Focus initial survey on repurchase intent, key attribute trade-offs, and competitive perception to directly measure loyalty
risks: Low response rates given no prior feedback culture — incentives may be needed
Marginally profitable company may have limited budget for extensive research
Survey design quality is critical; poorly designed questions will yield unreliable loyalty metrics
next_steps: Pilot the survey at 1-2 dealerships before rolling out to all 10
Establish a baseline loyalty score to track improvement over time
Create a closed-loop process to act on feedback so customers see tangible changes
